task.title: Check Out a Branch
task.shortdesc: Check out an existing branch, create a new one from a commit, or inspect a commit in a detached HEAD.

context.p: You check out from the view, starting from a chosen commit.

step.cmd: Right-click a commit in the view and select .

info.p: Double-clicking skips the dialog when the choice is unambiguous: double-click a commit row that has a single local branch to switch to that branch, or double-click directly on a branch label to switch to that specific branch.

choices.choice: Switch to existing local branch — checks out a branch that already points to the commit. This option appears only when one or more local branches point at the commit.
Create a new branch — enter a Branch name and, optionally, set it to track a remote branch. The Git Client pre-fills a suggested name and tracking when it can.
Detached HEAD — checks out the commit without a branch, for a quick look.

ul.li: An amber HEAD label marks the current commit while the repository is in detached HEAD mode. Any commits you create in this state are not on a branch, so create a branch before you switch away if you want to keep them easy to find.
To switch to an existing local branch from the view or the view, see .

result.p: The repository switches to the selected branch or commit. If you create a new branch, Git checks it out at the selected commit and applies the tracking configuration you selected. If you choose Detached HEAD, the repository remains in detached HEAD mode until you switch to a branch or create one.
